newsitem.title: UK: World nuclear body says safety has improved.
newsitem.headline: World nuclear body says safety has improved.

text.p: A nuclear industry body said on Tuesday that plant operators around the world had greatly improved safety this decade and the number of workers exposed to radiation had fallen sharply.

The World Association of Nuclear Operators, set up after the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, said falls in industrial accident rates, radiation exposure and automatic shutdowns had been accompanied by a rise in output capacities.

"If it (nuclear power) continues to make improvements in safety and reliability, I believe we will see a positive reappraisal of it as a viable source of energy in the next decade," said association chairman Remy Carle.
Exposure of plant workers to radiation has fallen 30 percent over the last five years, while accidents that resulted in one or more days off work have fallen by 60 percent since 1990, he said.
But Carle cautioned there was still much work to be done to improve safety, particularly in cash-strapped former eastern bloc countries with outdated plants.
The industry has striven to ensure safer nuclear power production and improve its image since the 1986 explosion at Chernobyl, Ukraine, which sent a lethal radioactive cloud across Europe.
All 436 of the world's commercial nuclear plants are members of the association.
Plant design, manufacture, and construction, along with staff competence and training, held the key to "safety culture", Carle said.
